title: Refactor coach skill with progressive disclosure approach
description:
The coach skill is becoming complex and monolithic. We need to refactor it to use a progressive disclosure approach for better performance, modularization, and maintainability.

CURRENT STATE:
- All functionality in a single SKILL.md file (~300 lines)
- References are included inline, making the file harder to navigate
- No clear separation of concerns between different features
- Hard to maintain and extend

DESIRED STATE:
- Progressive disclosure: Load core functionality first, lazy-load advanced/optional features
- Feature sets split across multiple md files with clear purposes
- Better organization for maintainability
- Improved performance by only loading what is needed

PROPOSED STRUCTURE:
- SKILL.md - Core coach identity, main workflow, essential guidelines only
- references/core.md - Core concepts that are always needed
- references/entity-detection.md - Entity detection and creation logic
- references/journaling.md - All diary/journal entry logic
- references/prioritization.md - Scoring algorithm and prioritization
- references/tts.md - Text-to-speech integration
- references/memory.md - Memory retrieval and vault reading logic

GOALS:
1. Modularize the skill into logical feature sets
2. Implement progressive loading (core first, features on-demand)
3. Improve maintainability through separation of concerns
4. Improve performance by lazy-loading less frequently used features
5. Make it easier to add new features without affecting core workflow

title: Refactor main skill description and logging logic
description: Refactor the main skill description to improve clarity and streamline logging decisions. The coach should have explicit, centralized logic for when to log and what to log. Add a dedicated Logging section to make logging behavior transparent and maintainable.

title: Create state module for settings management
description: Refactor the main skill into a new module called 'state'. This module should manage knowledge about what settings to load and when to use them, providing centralized state management for the coach.

title: Coach inserts past events on wrong journal page
description:
When the user mentions events that happened in the past (e.g., 'Yesterday I met with X', 'Last Monday I decided Y'), the coach currently writes those entries to today's journal page instead of the correct historical date's journal page.

Expected behavior:
- Parse date references from user statements (yesterday, last Monday, 3 days ago, specific dates like 'on January 10th')
- Insert diary entries on the correct historical journal page (e.g., {journals}/2026-01-10.md for 'on January 10th')
- Handle both relative dates (yesterday, last week) and absolute dates (January 10th, 2026-01-10)

Current behavior:
- All entries go to today's date regardless of when the event occurred

NOTE: There is existing functionality that attempts to handle past events (see SKILL.md lines 254-259 mentioning timestamp handling), but it does not appear to be working correctly. The coach still writes all entries to today's journal page even when the user explicitly mentions events from past dates.

title: Add optional location frontmatter attribute to projects
description: Introduce an optional but strongly recommended 'location' frontmatter attribute for projects. This field should point to a directory on disk. Having this accessible will allow the coach to dynamically read tasks from beads using the bd tool, enabling more flexible project exploration and task management.
